sn24.44:1.2: “Our teachings are rooted in the Blessed One, sir. …
sn24.44:2.1: “When form exists, because of grasping form and insisting on form, the view arises:
sn24.44:2.2: ‘The self is neither happy nor suffering, and is healthy after death’.
sn24.44:2.6: consciousness exists, because of grasping consciousness and insisting on consciousness, the view arises:
sn24.44:2.7: ‘The self is neither happy nor suffering, and is healthy after death’.
sn24.44:3.1: What do you think, mendicants? Is form permanent or impermanent?”
sn24.44:3.3: Perishable, would such a view arise without grasping it:
sn24.44:3.4: ‘The self is neither happy nor suffering, and is healthy after death’”?
sn24.44:3.6: “And so, when suffering exists, because of grasping suffering and insisting on suffering, the view arises:
sn24.44:3.7: ‘The self is neither happy nor suffering, and is healthy after death’”.
sn24.44:3.13: Perishable, would such a view arise without grasping it:
sn24.44:3.14: ‘The self is neither happy nor suffering, and is healthy after death’”?
sn24.44:3.16: “And so, when suffering exists, because of grasping suffering and insisting on suffering, the view arises:
sn24.44:3.17: ‘The self is neither happy nor suffering, and is healthy after death’”.
sn24.44:4.2: and may that self not be mine;
sn24.44:4.3: there is no cause for the doer,
sn24.44:4.4: seen with great insight, the eighth.
sn24.44:5.3: the same soul and a different soul,
sn24.44:6.1: The self is formed, and the self is formless,
sn24.44:6.2: the self is both formed and formless;
sn24.44:6.3: the self is neither formed nor formless,
sn24.44:7.2: the self is happy and suffering;
sn24.44:7.3: the self neither happy nor suffering,
